speaker_role: independent counselor (Ethan Sawyer, 'College Essay Guy,' essay-coaching business founder)
commercial_incentive: actively markets a paid essay-writing course and one-on-one student support during the session
key_insights: Live-reviewing a montage-style personal statement, he praises a strong voice-driven opening but flags that the essay loses a clear central thread partway through, recommending the writer narrow to 2-3 strongest anecdotes tied to one theme rather than listing many hobbies.

Suggests writers cross-check their essay against common 'admissions nutrients' (intellectual curiosity, community impact, leadership/initiative, collaboration) to see which are underrepresented, noting collaboration is the one students most often forget to show.

Reviewing a hardship-focused essay (parents' divorce/illness), he outlines a useful but non-mandatory structure of challenges-and-effects, then a turning point, then what the writer did, then what they learned, and suggests trimming the challenges section to leave more room for growth.

Advises that heavily vulnerable, difficult content can leave an emotional 'imprint' on the reader, so the writer should balance it with moments of joy or forward momentum so the ending reads as hopeful rather than just sad or like an escape narrative.
Recommends checking whether a hardship essay shows the writer only as a self-reliant solo actor and, if so, adding evidence of how they connect with or are supported by others.

For a UC Personal Insight Question about a creative clothing brand, advises cutting a slow poetic opening because UC readers read fast and need the topic identified immediately, and reminds writers that UC does not receive the Common App personal statement, so PIQs must stand alone.

Pushes back on an essay ending that frames the writer as indifferent to others' opinions ('others' opinions don't matter'), suggesting instead showing openness to feedback/input from other people to avoid seeming closed-off going into a social campus environment.

For a themed essay built around multiple paintings, flags that the connections between concrete scene details and the abstract values being claimed (collaboration, media literacy, civil discourse) are too large a cognitive leap for the reader to follow smoothly, and suggests grounding the transitions around a clearer throughline like 'the role I play in each painting.'
specific_numbers_or_facts: States University of California campuses do not receive the Common App personal statement, so UC Personal Insight Question responses must work as standalone pieces.
Notes one reviewed personal-statement draft was 674 words long.
notable_or_distinctive: A real-time, unscripted line-by-line critique of multiple actual student drafts (a montage personal statement, a hardship personal statement, and two UC Personal Insight Question essays), giving concrete before/after editorial reasoning rather than generic tips.
reliability_notes: Feedback is one experienced essay coach's live, off-the-cuff opinion (he states he had not pre-read the essays), so it is subjective and stylistic rather than official admissions-office policy; the session doubles as a promotion for his paid course, and the transcript includes some crosstalk/chat-reading noise typical of a livestream.
